sections.title: Taxes: what they are and why we pay them
How VAT moves along the chain

summary: VAT =(r)/(100)× price; bill = price ×(1+(r)/(100)); price = bill ÷(1+(r)/(100)). Nepal's standard rate is 13%.
Discount is allowed on the marked price first; VAT is charged on the selling price.
Excise duty is charged on the factory price; VAT is then charged on factory price + excise.
Final price with excise e% and VAT v%: factory ×(1+(e)/(100))(1+(v)/(100)).
A seller pays VAT collected on sales minus VAT paid on purchases.
Taxable income = total income - allowed deductions; tax is charged slab by slab at each slab's rate.
Foreign to rupees: multiply by the rate; rupees to foreign: divide. The bank's buying rate is lower than its selling rate.
INR 1 = Rs 1.6; convert one foreign currency to another through rupees.

Compound interest and simple interest compared

summary: Simple interest I=(PTR)/(100); compound interest adds interest to the principal every period.
A=Pleft(1+(R)/(100)right)^T and CI=A-P (compounded yearly).
Half-yearly: A=Pleft(1+(R)/(200)right)^2T; quarterly: A=Pleft(1+(R)/(400)right)^4T.
P=dfracA(1+R/100)^T; find R or T by matching A/P with a power.
For 2 years, CI-SI=Pleft((R)/(100)right)^2.
If the rate changes each year, multiply by each year's factor in turn.
More frequent compounding gives a larger amount.

sections.title: Growth and decay are repeated multiplications
Finding the rate or the time

summary: Growth: PT=P0left(1+(R)/(100)right)^T. Past population: divide by the factor.
Net rate = birth - death + immigration - emigration (all in % per year).
For different yearly rates multiply the factors; for a fixed number of migrants add or subtract at the correct time.
Depreciation: V=Pleft(1-(R)/(100)right)^T; total depreciation =P-V.
Depreciation each year is charged on the value at the start of that year, so the yearly loss shrinks.
Half-yearly: halve the rate and double the number of periods.
Find R or T by matching A/P (or V/P) with a power such as 1.1^2=1.21, 0.9^2=0.81, 0.8^2=0.64.
An increase of x% followed by a decrease of x% gives a net decrease.

Path or ring = larger area - smaller area; ring =π(R^2-r^2).
Path outside a rectangle adds 2w to each side; path inside subtracts 2w.
Combined figure: add areas; the joining line is not in the perimeter.
Cost = area (or length) × rate; number of tiles = floor area ÷ one tile.

units.title: Prism and Pyramid
summary: Right prism: LSA =Ph, TSA =Ph+2A, V=Ah (P base perimeter, A base area).
Cuboid: LSA =2h(l+b), TSA =2(lb+bh+hl), V=lbh, diagonal =√l^2+b^2+h^2.
Cube: TSA =6a^2, V=a^3.
Square pyramid: l^2=h^2+(frac a2)^2, LSA =2al, TSA =2al+a^2, V=frac13a^2h.
A pyramid is one third of the prism with the same base and height.
Cone: l^2=r^2+h^2, CSA =π rl, TSA =π r(r+l), V=frac13π r^2h.
1 dm³ =1 litre; 1 m³ =1000 litres.
The four walls of a room: 2h(l+b) minus the doors and windows.

sections.title: HCF and LCM of algebraic expressions
The relation between HCF, LCM and the expressions

summary: HCF = common factors at lowest powers; LCM = all factors at highest powers (include the numerical parts).
For two numbers or expressions: HCFtimesLCM=A× B. Not valid for three.
Factorisation toolkit: common factor, grouping, a^2-b^2, perfect squares, x^2+px+q, ax^2+bx+c, a^3± b^3.
Euclid's method: divide, then divide the divisor by the remainder, until the remainder is 0; the last divisor is the HCF.
Missing expression: B=dfracHCFtimesLCMA.
A letter missing from any one term is not in the HCF.
Word problems: HCF for equal cutting; LCM for common times.

sections.title: Values of expressions: x+(1)/(x) and its powers

summary: A surd √[n]a (a rational) is irrational; √16, √[3]27 are not surds; √2, √[3]5 are.
√a×√b=√ab; frac√a√b=√frac ab; (√a)^2=a; but √a+b≠√a+√b.
Add and subtract only like surds after simplifying: 5√2+3√2=8√2.
Conjugate of a+√b is a-√b; product =a^2-b (rational).
Rationalise frac1√a by √a; rationalise frac1√a±√b by √amp√b, giving denominator a-b.
Compare surds of different order by writing both with the LCM of the indices.

units.title: Indices
summary: a^m× a^n=a^m+n, a^m÷ a^n=a^m-n, (a^m)^n=a^mn, (ab)^n=a^nb^n.
a^0=1 and a^-n=(1)/(a^n); a negative index flips the base.
a^1/n is the nth root of a and a^m/n=left(a^1/nright)^m: root first, then power.
If a^x=a^y (a>0, a≠1) then x=y.
To solve an exponential equation: common base, simplify, equate indices, check.
For sums like a^x+k± a^x take the smallest power as the common factor.
Equations such as 4^x-5·2^x+4=0: put y=2^x and solve the quadratic in y.
To prove an identity: simplify one side with the laws until it equals the other.

units.title: Algebraic Fraction
summary: Factorisation formulas: a^2-b^2=(a+b)(a-b); (a± b)^2; a^3± b^3=(a± b)(a^2mp ab+b^2); trinomials by sum and product or by splitting the middle term.
Cancel only factors, never added terms.
To add or subtract: factorise the denominators, take the LCM, rewrite, combine numerators with brackets, simplify.
Complex fractions: simplify the inside first; x^2-(1)/(x^2)=left(x+(1)/(x)right)left(x-(1)/(x)right).
Fractional equations: multiply by the LCM; reject roots that zero a denominator.
Always check with a small number such as x=2.

Reject answers that are impossible in the context.
When squaring an equation containing a square root, check every root in the original.

summary: Parallelograms on the same base and between the same parallels have equal area.
A triangle on the same base as a parallelogram and between the same parallels has half its area.
Triangles on the same base (or equal bases) and between the same parallels are equal in area.
A median divides a triangle into two triangles of equal area; triangles with the same height have areas in the ratio of their bases.
The diagonals of a parallelogram divide it into four triangles of equal area.
Formulas: parallelogram bh; triangle (1)/(2)bh; trapezium (1)/(2)(a+b)h; rhombus (1)/(2)d1d2; quadrilateral (1)/(2)d(h1+h2).

summary: Constructions use only a ruler and compass (a protractor only for a given angle); keep all arcs.
Parallel through a point: rhombus method with equal radii.
Triangle = quadrilateral: join diagonal AC; through D draw DE∥ AC meeting BC produced at E; Δ ABE has the same area.
Parallelogram = triangle: bisect the base; draw the given angle at the midpoint; parallels through the apex and through the end of the base.

summary: sinθ=(p)/(h), cosθ=(b)/(h), tanθ=(p)/(b)=(sinθ)/(cosθ); reciprocals csc,sec,cot. Memory aid SOH-CAH-TOA.
Standard values for 30^°,45^°,60^° come from the triangles with sides 1,1,√2 and 1,√3,2.
Complementary angles: sin(90^°-θ)=cosθ, cos(90^°-θ)=sinθ, tan(90^°-θ)=cotθ.
Identities: sin^2θ+cos^2θ=1; 1+tan^2θ=sec^2θ; 1+cot^2θ=csc^2θ.

units.title: Statistics
summary: Range =L-S; coefficient (L-S)/(L+S).
Q1 at (n+1)/(4)th item, Q3 at (3(n+1))/(4)th item (individual/discrete); (n)/(4), (3n)/(4) with the interpolation formula for continuous data.
QD=(Q3-Q1)/(2); coefficient (Q3-Q1)/(Q3+Q1).
MD=(Σ f|x-bar x|)/(n); coefficient (MD)/(bar x).
σ=√(Σ f(x-bar x)^2)/(n)=√(Σ fx^2)/(n)-bar x^2; step deviation σ=h√(Σ fd'^2)/(n)-left((Σ fd')/(n)right)^2.
CV=(σ)/(bar x)×100%; the smaller CV is the more consistent.
Adding a constant leaves σ unchanged; multiplying by k multiplies σ by |k|.

units.title: Probability
topics: Independent events and the multiplication rule

sections.title: Independent events and the multiplication rule

summary: P(E)=(n(E))/(n(S)) for equally likely outcomes; 0≤ P(E)≤1.
Complement: P(E')=1-P(E). "At least one" =1-P(none).
Addition rule: P(A∪ B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A∩ B); for mutually exclusive events P(A∩ B)=0.
Multiplication rule for independent events: P(A∩ B)=P(A)× P(B).
Without replacement the second probability changes; use a tree diagram and multiply along each path.
Two dice: 36 outcomes; two coins: 4; three coins: 8; pack of cards: 52.
Expected frequency =N× P(E).
